content: To accurately diagnose obesity, it is essential to calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) by measuring an individual's height and weight. In addition to BMI, other anthropometric measurements, such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio, should be assessed to better understand the distribution of body fat. These additional measurements are particularly valuable because they provide insights into the risk factors for cardiovascular and metabolic complications associated with obesity. Abdominal fat, in particular, is more strongly linked to health risks compared to fat distributed in other areas of the body. It is recommended that BMI and these supplementary measurements be monitored at least once a year. This regular monitoring allows for the tracking of changes in obesity status and enables timely adjustments to treatment plans as needed.
